title: Always Equal 1? Trig Identities Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Sine squared plus cosine squared. Secant squared minus tan squared. Cosecant squared minus cot squared. Three expressions that look nothing alike, yet for any angle you try, all three give exactly 1. Luck, or a law? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 3, Trigonometric Functions) we prove all three trigonometric identities from one unit circle.

You will see what makes an identity different from an equation, watch a live angle slider keep sin²θ + cos²θ at 1.000 in every quadrant, see Pythagoras as two small squares filling a big one, and stretch the same triangle to get 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ. Two pause-and-think questions, a worked example (find tan, sin and cosec from sec θ = 13/5 in quadrant IV), the exam trap with (sin θ + cos θ)², an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Three expressions, one answer
0:29 Equation or identity?
1:02 The unit circle and a live angle
1:24 Proof: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
2:10 Identity 2: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ
2:47 Identity 3: 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ
2:59 Where each identity holds
3:37 Worked example: sec θ = 13/5 in quadrant IV
4:26 Exam trap: (sin θ + cos θ)²
4:44 Where it is asked
4:50 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:27 Recap and three questions to answer
